title: Architecture Review - KV Cache Sharding & Routing (Meeting Notes)
summary: Notes from architecture review on KV cache sharding and request routing. Focus: alignment on shard key, routing policy, fallback behavior, and rollout plan to meet latency SLOs while enabling multi-tenant isolation.
content:
Agenda:
- Recap of RFC goals and constraints
- Proposed shard key designs (model+customer vs prefix hash)
- Routing policy and fallback (latency-first vs cost-first)
- Consistency, cache warming, and KV cache eviction semantics
- Rollout strategy and telemetry needs

Discussion notes:
- Background: current single-shard KV cache causes tail latency spikes when one tenant issues many long-context requests. RFC proposes sharding the KV cache across GPU workers and introducing a routing layer that pins requests to shards to maximize cache hit locality.

- Shard Key options:
  1) model_id + customer_id: gives strong tenant isolation and model-specific locality. Pros: good isolation for enterprise customers, simpler quota/metric attribution. Cons: may create sparse hot shards for small customers; requires more metadata on requests.
  2) prefix-hash (first N tokens hash): better distribution for bursty single large-tenant workloads, but risk of mixing tenants on same shard (affects isolation).
  3) hybrid: prefer model+customer when present, fallback to prefix-hash for anonymous/hosted requests. Provides a middle-ground.

- Performance tradeoffs:
  - Priya presented simulated hit-rate curves: model+customer gives 15-22% higher hit rate for multi-tenant workloads in our traces; prefix-hash evens out load but loses some locality.
  - Liam emphasized memory pressure and per-shard KV index size: we should cap per-shard entries and implement proportional eviction across tenants to avoid noisy-neighbor thrash.

- Routing policy decisions:
  - Two primary policy modes: latency-first (route to shard with warmed cache even if cost higher), cost-first (route to cheapest available shard).
  - Consensus: default = latency-first for enterprise SLO-bound customers; cost-first for free-tier/anonymous requests. Routing policy should be configurable per-route and per-customer.

- Fallbacks and graceful degradation:
  - If the pinned shard is overloaded/unavailable, plan is: 1) try fallback to another shard with compatible model variant, 2) if no warmed shard, run request on a cold shard but mark as cold-serve for telemetry, 3) if overall capacity exhausted, apply rate-limit or degrade to lower-context model variant.
  - Sofia noted that fallback must preserve request ordering for multi-turn chat; implement request-local KV stamping to avoid inconsistency when switching shards mid-conversation.

- Consistency & Eviction:
  - We will keep KV entries eventually consistent across shards only for replicated entries (rare). Primary model will be single-writer per key (the shard that originally observed the prefix). Eviction policy: LRU with tenant-weighted quotas.

- Security & Multi-tenant isolation:
  - Ravi: enforce strict memory/key boundaries per customer in enterprise mode. Add KMS-scoped metadata tags for private deployments.

- Observability and Telemetry:
  - Required metrics: per-shard hit-rate, per-customer hit-rate, cold-serve count, fallback frequency, tail latency percentiles by route, and per-shard memory utilization.
  - Logging: inject shard_id and routing_decision into traces. Add a metric for "cross-shard conversation switches" to detect ordering regressions.

- Rollout plan:
  - Phase 1 (canary): small percentage of traffic for non-production customers and internal staging — enable model+customer shard key, latency-first policy. Collect telemetry for 2 weeks.
  - Phase 2 (broader internal): expand to all internal + select customers, enable eviction quotas and fallback paths. 1 month observation.
  - Phase 3 (gradual public): opt-in for customers, then automatic for enterprise tiers. Monitor SLOs closely; have a fast rollback path.

Decisions (recorded):
- Adopt hybrid shard key: prefer model_id+customer_id when available, fallback to prefix-hash for anonymous/hosted requests. (Decision owner: Priya)
- Default routing policy: latency-first for enterprise routes; cost-first for free-tier. Routing policy to be configurable per-route/customer. (Decision owner: Jordan)
- Eviction policy: tenant-weighted LRU with per-tenant soft quotas; global cap per-shard. (Decision owner: Liam)
- Fallback sequence: warmed-shard -> compatible-shard -> cold-serve -> degrade-to-variant/rate-limit. Mark cold serves in telemetry. (Decision owner: Sofia)

Open questions / risks:
- How to handle long-running multi-turn chats that cross shards due to prefix evolution? (Action: prototype request-local KV stamping to preserve ordering)
- Quantifying cost delta between latency-first vs cost-first for peak traffic — need more traces.
- Operational complexity: shard rebalancing when tenant footprint changes. Could require live migration; explore lightweight lease-based transfer or rebuild-from-warm-start.

Action items:
- Priya: run extended trace sims comparing hybrid shard key vs prefix-hash-only across 30 days of production traces; present results by 2026-03-10.
- Liam: prototype tenant-weighted LRU eviction with global cap in staging; include memory metrics. ETA 2026-03-05.
- Sofia: add shard_id and routing_decision fields to tracing instrumentation and create dashboard skeleton. ETA 2026-03-03.
- Ravi: draft security notes for enterprise-mode isolation and KMS metadata patterns. ETA 2026-03-08.
- Jordan: author short RFC appendix documenting rollout phases and rollback playbook; share with SRE and product. ETA 2026-03-04.
